sections.heading: Big-Company Products, Owners on the Job
body: The outside of your house is one system. Windows, siding, doors and trim all meet at the same edges.
A leak or a draft at one shows up as a problem at the others. That's why we do all of it, and why one of us comes out to look before anyone quotes a price.
We don't spend on big ad campaigns, so that cost stays out of your price.
You get a real look at what's wrong and a price with no pressure to sign that day. Do the whole exterior at once, or one project at a time.
And because we're a small company, the people who quote your job are the people you call if anything isn't right.

sections.heading: Replacement Windows
body: Most of our work is windows. People usually call us because of a room that never gets comfortable, curtains that move with the window shut, fog between the panes, or a sash that sticks.
Each one points to a window that has stopped sealing. You're paying to heat and cool the outdoors through it.

We measure every opening, show you the window up close and order each one to fit. In older Wichita houses, we'll show you where two or three small windows could become one larger one: more light, fewer windows to buy.
Most homes are done in a day. Our energy efficient windows carry a manufacturer's lifetime warranty, from glass breakage to how the window opens and closes.
Casement, double hung, sliding, awning, hopper, picture, bay and basement windows.

sections.quote: Our basement windows were so old and worn out that we could hear the neighbor dog barking like it was in our house. Our new windows were just installed and it is night and day different. We can't hear a PEEP! No dogs, no lawn mowers, no thunderstorms.. NOTHING!

sections.heading: Vinyl Siding
body: Siding takes the Kansas wind, hail and summer sun before anything else on the house does.
When it's worn out, you see it: faded or chalky panels, cracks, warped or melted spots, pieces the wind keeps loosening. What you don't see is the wall behind it, where gaps let in drafts and water.
We'll tell you straight whether yours has years left or is failing. If it was put up badly in the first place, patching it only buys time.
A siding consultation takes about an hour. We look at the whole house, talk through colors and styles, and give you the price. When the new siding goes up, the old siding leaves with us.

body: An old sliding door is usually the leakiest opening in the house. The rollers wear out, the track bends, and the seal where the panels meet stops sealing.
You end up shoving it open with your shoulder and feeling the draft all winter. A new slider glides on new rollers and seals tight when it's closed.
We install it on its own or with your new windows, so the glass and frames match.

sections.heading: Signs Your Windows Are Costing You
body: Most people don't replace windows on a whim. Something tips them off. These are the problems we hear about most, and what each one usually means:
list: **Curtains move when the window is shut.** Air is getting past worn seals or a frame that has shifted. You're paying to heat and cool the outdoors.
**Fog or haze between the panes.** The seal that holds the insulating gas between the panes has failed. The window has lost most of its insulating value, and it won't clear up on its own.
**One room is always hotter or colder than the rest.** Old single-pane glass and thin frames let summer sun and winter cold straight through. West-facing rooms feel it first in a Kansas July.
**You can hear the street, the neighbor's dog, the train.** Sound comes in through the same gaps air does. Sealed, multi-pane glass quiets a house more than most people expect.
**Sashes that stick, won't lock or won't stay open.** Worn balances and warped frames. In an older house it's rarely just one window.
tail: If it's one or two windows, replace those and stop there. If it's most of the house, we'll show you what doing it all at once costs next to doing it in stages, and you choose.

sections.heading: Window Styles, and Where Each One Earns Its Place
body: We install casement, double hung, sliding, awning, hopper, picture, bay and basement windows. The right one depends on the opening and how you use the room.
list: **Double hung** is the familiar up-and-down window, and it fits most older Wichita houses without changing how the front looks.
**Casement** windows crank out on a hinge. They seal tightly when closed and catch a breeze when open.
**Sliding** windows suit wide, low openings where there's no room to swing a sash.
**Awning and hopper** windows hinge at the top or bottom, so you can leave them open a crack without letting rain in.
**Picture** windows are fixed glass: the most light and the fewest parts to wear out.
**Bay** windows push out from the wall and give a living or dining room its view.
tail: At your consultation you also choose colors, hardware and grids, so the windows look like they belong to your house.

sections.quote: Colton helped me find the perfect windows for my 1948 house! Every window in the house was replaced with exactly what I wanted and his quote was less than the three other quotes I had gotten. … I'm VERY picky and he was patient and attentive to all the details that I wanted, from oil rubbed bronze hardware to custom grids on the front windows.

sections.heading: Fewer, Bigger Windows Where They Make Sense
body: Older Wichita houses were often built with rows of small windows: three narrow units where one wide one would do.

When we measure, we look at every opening and ask whether it should stay the way it was built. Combining two or three small windows into one larger one gives you more glass and a cleaner look from the street.
It also means fewer windows to buy and install, which can take a real bite out of the price of the job. We show you both versions and you decide.

So we measure every opening and order each window to fit it. Then we finish the trim so the new window looks like it was always there.
Before anything comes out, we cover and protect your house and yard.

sections.heading: Siding Takes the Weather First
body: Before the windows, the doors or the roof edge feel a Kansas storm, the siding has already taken it. Wind, hail and summer sun hit it every year.
It rarely fails all at once. It fades, loosens and cracks a little at a time, and the real damage happens behind it, where gaps let in drafts and water.

sections.heading: What Worn-Out Siding Looks Like
body: Here is what to look for, and what each sign usually means:
list: **Faded or chalky panels.** The finish has worn off in the sun. Rub a hand across it and the color comes off as powder.
**Cracks and hail dings.** Vinyl turns brittle with age. A crack lets water behind the panel.
**Warped or melted spots.** Panels that have buckled or sagged have been pushed past what they can take, often by heat or by being fastened too tight.
**Pieces the wind keeps loosening.** Panels that rattle or lift in a storm have lost their hold on the wall.
**Gaps at corners and around windows.** This is where air and water find their way in.
**Energy bills creeping up.** Siding that no longer seals the wall lets the house leak heat all winter and gain it all summer.
tail: If you see two or three of these, it's time to have someone look at the whole wall.

sections.heading: Does Yours Have Years Left?
body: We'll tell you straight. If your siding is sound, we'll say so.
If it was put up badly in the first place, patching it only buys time. Panels fastened too tight or hung crooked will keep failing, no matter how many you swap out.

sections.heading: What New Vinyl Siding Does for the House
body: Vinyl doesn't need painting, and a wash with a hose is most of the upkeep. That makes it a good fit for the part of the house you'd rather not think about.
It also helps your energy bills. New panels that lock together tight leave fewer gaps for air and water, so the house holds its heat in winter and keeps more of the summer out.
You choose the colors and styles with us at your consultation, with the trim and windows in mind.

Your customers already make your case. You hold a 5.0 on 140 Google reviews, and they say it plainly: "Small company with owner involvement." "My house is much quieter and cooler now." "If you are looking into getting new windows call Evolve Exteriors first!"
Your website hides all of it behind sample text, and its phone buttons reach neither office.
So we built this site around their words.

strategy.cardsIntro: Each card is one page: what your site does today and what we changed.

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: The page Google reads to learn who you are and where you work.
problems: Every call button dials 1234567890, so a visitor who taps your Wichita number reaches nothing.
The Oklahoma City number is plain text with no button, so your second office can't be reached by tap.
The top of the page says "Best Professional Window Installation" with no town, so Google can't tell you work in Wichita.
Your 140 reviews are missing; the only quote is sample text from "Samantha Johnson".
fixes: Wichita and Oklahoma City are each one tap to call, on every page.
A headline that says exterior remodeling company in Wichita, KS, right at the top.
Real reviews from your customers, each beside the point it proves.
cards.alsoAdd: On day one, we sit down with you to get what makes you the obvious choice, every service you offer and every town you work in. That becomes the prescription: how many pages, in how many towns, so Google and AI tools can find you for every service.

cards.title: Window Replacement
cards.why: Windows are about three quarters of your written reviews, and they have no real page.
problems: "Our Windows" is eight style names with nothing on warranty, price or install, so Google has little to rank and shoppers little reason to call.
fixes: A full page for window replacement in Wichita, KS: styles, warranty, price match and install day.
Reviews on basement windows, old houses and cooler rooms, each beside its point.
cards.alsoAdd: Pages planned from what Google actually shows for each search, so every page targets something people really look for.

Your siding reviews beside the work they describe.
